t: The Ritual vs. The Decorator: A Battle for Token Efficiency
s: This article explores optimizing the Pipulate framework for AI collaboration by debating design choices. It contrasts the author's explicit 'WET' approach with AI-suggested 'DRY' patterns, focusing on token efficiency and cognitive load for AI coding assistants.
sub: Pipulate framework's 'WET' philosophy vs. AI's 'DRY' suggestions
AI's 'Burr Analysis' of codebase: monolithic classes, docstring paradox, numbered plugins, repetitive 'pip = self.pipulate' ritual, state management complexity
Proposed AI-delightful improvements: semantic file organization, single responsibility functions, config over code, consistent error handling, observable patterns
Author's defense of deliberate 'anti-patterns' for competitive advantage and explicitness, prioritizing developer and AI understanding
Debate on decorator pattern as a compromise for ritual elimination without violating core principles
